close_reason: ValidationPolicy::new(now_unix) is the preferred constructor and is documented. Default has a comment noting current_time_unix=0 requires explicit setting. Removing Default is a breaking API change deferred to v0.2.
description: ValidationPolicy::default() sets current_time_unix=0 (1970-01-01). Any caller who writes ValidationPolicy { max_path_len: 5, ..Default::default() } will silently get time=0 and fail all cert validity checks with ValidityPeriod. The rustdoc warning on the field is good, but the Default impl itself is the trap: Rust developers habitually use ..Default::default() without reading field docs. Issue reports from this will be chronic. Mitigation options: (a) remove Default impl and force explicit construction, (b) make ValidationPolicy::new(now) the only public path and mark Default as deprecated, or (c) add a builder pattern. The current ValidationPolicy::new(now_unix) constructor is the right UX — Default should be removed or panic-guarded.
title: ValidationPolicy::default() current_time_unix=0 is a footgun
